calls.reason: TechCrunch reports improving Cursor margins and fundraising; Stripe reports profitable growth at Gamma. Neither establishes whether the largest customers, or every relevant startup, need increasing outside funding.

Independently verified reporting puts OpenAI's 2025 net loss at $38.5 billion; Anthropic's filing reports $42 billion. Both support the headline loss claim, although large noncash charges limit its implications for cash needs.

The Next Web reports substantial OpenAI liquidity, and Anthropic discloses major financing and fixed commitments. Without payment schedules, these do not establish affordability or dependence on low signing costs.
Ramp shows paid adoption spreading across non-tech sectors, but does not show how many such businesses spend substantial amounts. Its spending figures cannot settle the claim's main point.

Ramp's economist directly reports the 80% concentration among 1% of customers and says it is not improving. This supports the main point within the acknowledged sample, although the three-year duration remains unverified.

Meta reports operating cash covering quarterly capital expenditure, alongside substantial debt. One quarter does not settle sustained borrowing needs, and the packet does not measure a price-driven contraction in buyers.
